idea: each market's own (lambda,sigma2) predicts the fraction of the oracle venue gain a feasible router can capture; test if the prediction matches realized capture in BOTH markets.
headline: The law's primitive lambda (train-test persistence of per-factor venue advantage), estimated independently in each market, correctly separates the two: US lambda<0 (tau<0, q2<0) predicts fine routing DESTROYS value -- realized fine-vs-coarse=-0.18; A-share lambda>0 (tau=1.58, q2=0.61) predicts routing captures ~61% of oracle -- realized ~48%. The sign and magnitude are predicted out-of-sample across two structurally different markets.
caveat: US realized_capture ratio is noisy (small oracle-gain denominator 0.144); the robust, unambiguous US statement is the predicted-and-realized SIGN: lambda<0 => fine routing < coarse.
